brief: Hartnett's weekly BofA Flow Show, covered by Zero Hedge, traces how Tuesday's Democratic sweep triggered Thursday's "Fireworks Day" crash (Nasdaq's worst day since Covid, a record Cboe put-volume day), which hit the AI junk bonds Hartnett had told clients to buy just a week earlier, as incoming Democratic governors' promised data-center moratoria repriced AI capex risk. Texas's governor-elect campaigned on a freeze, 76% of voters oppose nearby data centers, and Goldman now expects moratoria to freeze about 45% of planned US capacity, pressuring the $1.3tn of 2027 hyperscaler capex consensus and its -$252bn free cash flow forecast. Hartnett still prefers tech bonds over tech stocks, reasoning that slower, better-funded capex should eventually help creditors. Politically he reads the sweep as a shift from populist capitalism to populist socialism, raising tax/regulation risk, and dates the AI Big 10's 41% market-cap concentration peak to the midterms. His three recession canaries are mixed (banks hold, junk barely holds, mid-caps already broke), and Friday's hot jobs report killed his near-term risk-rally case, leaving him recommending gold into the looming debt-ceiling fight while advising to sell oil, buy bonds and wait.
